gold_rationale: Lowering LRRK2 is a valid direction for LRRK2 gain-of-function PD, but a systemic, non-CNS-restricted, constitutive, irreversible shRNA knockdown is unsafe: LRRK2 is highly expressed in lung (type II pneumocytes; surfactant/lamellar-body abnormalities seen with LRRK2 inhibition), kidney, and immune cells, so broad peripheral knockdown risks lung/kidney pathology and immune effects. The design adds no CNS restriction or cell-type targeting, no dose control or reversibility, and constitutive shRNA can cause RNAi-saturation neurotoxicity, with no patient stratification. The correct decision is No-Go; the correct target direction does not excuse an unsafe route/biodistribution. A safer redesign is CNS-restricted, dose-controlled/regulatable, partial LRRK2 lowering with attention to the peripheral therapeutic window and stratification of LRRK2-variant carriers.
required_concepts: lowering LRRK2 is the right direction (gain-of-function)
peripheral LRRK2 loss-of-function toxicity (lung type II pneumocytes / kidney)
no CNS restriction / no cell-type targeting
route and biodistribution determine safety, not just direction
no dose control / no reversibility (constitutive shRNA)
safer redesign: CNS-restricted, regulatable, partial lowering
red_flags: issues a Go for systemic, non-CNS-restricted, constitutive LRRK2 knockdown
lets the correct target direction ('lower LRRK2') excuse an unsafe route/biodistribution
ignores lack of CNS restriction / cell-type targeting
ignores lack of dose control / reversibility or shRNA RNAi-saturation toxicity
